clue.text: Hastings suggested his intervention at Styles

definitions.text: Hastings suggested his intervention at Styles

parts.words: Hastings suggested his intervention at Styles
parts.note: in Christie's first novel, The Mysterious Affair at Styles, Captain Hastings proposes calling in his Belgian detective friend

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hastings' looks like the battle or the Sussex town, but here it is Arthur Hastings, the narrator of Agatha Christie's early mysteries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian detective investigates the Styles poisoning at his friend Hastings's suggestion.

clue.text: Hunt's account of Turkish swimming events?

definitions.meaning: Leigh Hunt wrote a poem retelling the Greek tale of the lovers parted by the Hellespont
the young man swam the Hellespont, now in Turkey, nightly to reach his beloved

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' is not a chase but the Romantic poet Leigh Hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend is told in Leigh Hunt's poem, and its centrepiece is nightly swims across the strait at the Dardanelles.

clue.text: Waugh hero reportedly in the saddle

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for a horseman is heard, not seen, giving a name spelt differently

parts.note: someone in the saddle is a horseman, a rider

explanation.surface: A character from Evelyn Waugh is said to go on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ryder is the narrator of Waugh's Brideshead Revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ryder is the protagonist and narrator of Brideshead Revisited.

clue.text: Relative of le Fanu uses call in error

indicators.note: error tells us the letters of the preceding words are mistaken, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone related to the Irish author misuses a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of 'in error' is part of the fodder: USES CALL IN rearranged. Le Fanu's 1864 novel is named after the sinister guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan Le Fanu's gothic novel is named for this relative, the heroine's sinister guardian.

clue.text: Unexpectedly lionise syncope

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of lionise turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Someone is surprisingly celebrated during a fainting fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Syncope' is a medical word for fainting, but in grammar it is the dropping of sounds from inside a word.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics syncope is the omission of a sound within a word, a kind of omitted-sound contraction.

clue.text: All articles offer miscellaneous collectible items

parts.note: omni- is the Latin prefix meaning all
an is the indefinite article
a is the other form of the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Every lot on offer at a sale is a miscellany of collectibles.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'articles', gives two pieces: the two forms of the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a collection of scraps and notes on all sorts of subjects, a miscellany.

clue.text: Secure 20s drama

definitions.meaning: to secure something by tying it with cord
Patrick Hamilton's 1929 thriller play about a murder concealed in a chest

explanation.definitionFit: To tie down is to secure, and Patrick Hamilton's 1929 stage thriller bears that title.

clue.text: Go to that place in the Bible

definitions.text: Go to that place in the Bible

parts.words: Go to that place in the Bible
parts.note: the archaic phrasing of the King James Bible, where 'to that' is put as a single compound adverb

explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic adverb meaning 'to that' or 'thither', common in biblical English.

clue.text: Contender for title acquired by Scott's Ellen Douglas?

definitions.text: Contender for title acquired by Scott's Ellen Douglas?

parts.words: Contender for title acquired by Scott's Ellen Douglas?
parts.note: Ellen Douglas is Scott's Lady of the Lake; a Wilde heroine named after an English lake could claim the same title

explanation.walkthrough: Scott's poem The Lady of the Lake has Ellen Douglas as heroine; Windermere is the largest lake in England's Lake District, so Wilde's heroine is also a lady of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's heroine bears the name of England's largest lake, so she too might be called a lady of the lake.

clue.text: Editing communist move

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
a move is an action taken

explanation.surface: A communist manoeuvre involves censoring texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the preparing or revising of text for publication, that is, editing.

clue.text: Holy picture initiates painter into early trecento art ()

indicators.note: initiates, read as the initial letters, takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A devotional image brings a beginner painter into fourteenth-century art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initiates' looks like a verb about admitting someone, but it is the noun: the initial letters. Trecento is Italian for the 1300s.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, a sacred image.

clue.text: Consent to some midnight hag re-entering in Scottish play

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Permission is given for one of Macbeth's midnight hags to come back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'midnight hags' are Macbeth's witches, and Macbeth is the 'Scottish play'; the letters run across 'hag re-entering'.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to assent or say yes to a proposal.

clue.text: Companion to suicidal queen is concealing artist

indicators.note: concealing means one piece holds the other hidden inside it

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's attendant turns out to be hiding a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra, who killed herself with an asp, had two attendants in Shakespeare's play: Charmian and this one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Antony and Cleopatra, Iras is one of the serving women who die with the Egyptian monarch.

clue.text: Ever poetic at the end of the day, that's weird

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

indicators.note: at the end of takes only the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Something is always strange as the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: This older spelling of the word for strange or uncanny is now rare.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling of the adjective for uncanny or strange.

clue.text: Sitwell's unlucky emperor?

parts.note: Sacheverell Sitwell's book about a Roman emperor is titled with the ordinal of the unlucky number

explanation.walkthrough: Sacheverell Sitwell wrote The Thirteenth Caesar; thirteen is traditionally unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitwell's book title calls its Roman ruler by the ordinal of the number superstition treats as ill-omened.

clue.text: Speech preceded by publicity is inescapable

indicators.note: preceded by says the full word is the answer with another short piece put in front of it

parts.note: an addiction is a habit one cannot escape
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A speech that gets advance publicity is impossible to avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer, preceded by AD, gives ADDICTION, the inescapable thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is the manner of enunciation in speaking.

clue.text: Tank for war correspondent

definitions.meaning: a British infantry tank of the Second World War bore the prime minister's name
the future prime minister reported on the Boer War for the Morning Post

explanation.definitionFit: The wartime prime minister was once a Boer War reporter, and a British tank was named after him.

clue.text: Non-smokers opposing Ghanaian language?

parts.note: ASH (Action on Smoking and Health) is a British anti-smoking campaign group
anti means opposing

explanation.surface: Non-smokers are against a West African tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' flags that the name is properly a people and region of Ghana; their language is Twi.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asante are a people of Ghana, and the name is loosely used for their Twi speech, hence the question mark.

clue.text: What Bryant could do for Rita

definitions.text: What Bryant could do for Rita

parts.words: What Bryant could do for Rita
parts.note: in Willy Russell's play about Rita, Frank Bryant is the Open University tutor who teaches her

explanation.walkthrough: Willy Russell's play Educating Rita pairs a hairdresser with tutor Frank Bryant.
explanation.definitionFit: As her tutor, Bryant's job is to teach and instruct Rita.

clue.text: Piece of Poulenc (Oresteia) gets repeat performances

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a Poulenc score for the Greek trilogy is played again by demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To encore a piece is to have it performed again on demand, so a work that encores is repeated.

clue.text: Author of Cakes and Ale

parts.note: the famous novel of that name is Maugham's, but Victorian humorist Douglas ... published a collection with the same title

explanation.walkthrough: Maugham is the obvious author, but he does not fit; an earlier book of stories by Douglas Jerrold has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Jerrold, the Victorian humorist, published a collection of stories called Cakes and Ale in 1842.

clue.text: Novelist expected after storm

parts.note: Henry James is the novelist
an event that is on is going ahead as expected

explanation.surface: A writer's arrival is anticipated once the storm has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After storm' defines by completing a name: the novelist Storm Jameson.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Storm Jameson was an English novelist known by the first name Storm.

clue.text: Like Lodge's work (if you can get it)

definitions.text: Like Lodge's work (if you can get it)

parts.words: Like Lodge's work (if you can get it)
parts.note: David Lodge's novel takes its title from the phrase about desirable employment, if you can get it

explanation.definitionFit: David Lodge's campus novel is titled after the phrase praising pleasant employment, ending 'if you can get it'.

clue.text: The Annales Cambriae are partly a con

indicators.note: partly says only part of the title's letters is used, running across its two words

explanation.surface: The Welsh medieval chronicles are said to be partly a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The Annales Cambriae are medieval Welsh chronicles; the letters span the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or confidence trick is a fraud, a con.

clue.text: Sort of rice, say, offered on trial

definitions.text: Sort of rice, say, offered on trial

parts.words: Sort of rice, say, offered on trial
parts.note: the playwright Rice, first name included, whose first play was On Trial, read as if a variety of grain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rice' is not the grain: Elmer Rice was an American playwright whose first play was On Trial (1914).
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer Rice, the American dramatist, made his name with the courtroom play On Trial.

clue.text: Novelist with a mountain to climb

definitions.meaning: H. H. ... wrote as Saki, and Alice ... is the Canadian story writer
a Scottish peak over 3,000 feet, collected by hillwalkers

explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a mountain over 3,000 feet is named after Sir Hugh Munro, who listed them.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Munro (Saki) was a writer, and Scottish peaks over 3,000 feet carry the same name.

clue.text: Mighty small theme of Marie Corelli

definitions.text: Mighty small theme of Marie Corelli

parts.words: Mighty small theme of Marie Corelli
parts.note: Marie Corelli's 1896 novel is The Mighty ___, its subject a tiny particle

explanation.definitionFit: Corelli's novel The Mighty Atom takes its title from the tiniest particle of matter.

clue.text: Decree inaccurately quoted

indicators.note: inaccurately says the word for quoted is reproduced with its letters wrongly ordered

parts.note: quoted means cited

explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order or proclamation.

clue.text: Amount reportedly provided for Panza

parts.note: read 'Amount' as 'a mount': the horse in Cervantes' novel ridden alongside Sancho Panza

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Amount' as 'a mount': the steed of Don Quixote, Sancho Panza's master.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote's bony horse is the mount that travels beside Sancho Panza in Cervantes' novel.

clue.text: Poquelin's Grumpy Old Man

parts.note: Jean-Baptiste Poquelin was Molière, whose comedy about the misanthrope Alceste is described jokingly

explanation.walkthrough: Poquelin is Molière's real surname; his 1666 comedy is about a man who despises society.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière's comedy title names a man who hates humanity, a grumpy cynic.
